items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...Chris Kelly in there?... [INTERVIEWEE] ...I remember Buddy around here...

ctx.x: Oh, yeah, yeah. I started out reading, yeah. Yeah.

How about the banjos in the old rougher type bands, you know, the dancehall bands like Buddy Petit and Chris Kelly in there? What did the banjo players in there, did they differ from your type of playing?

Well, each guy had his particular style and playing, you know. Some guys I know, probably they couldn't solo, but sometimes leaders, some leaders wouldn't even permit banjo to solos, you know. Like I said, those days I remember the solo number was well, waiting for the sunrise, and Tiger Rag, you know, that was a muscle and a banjo.

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: Man, Chris Kelly, boy, could play your old blues on that. He was the best, he was the best on that.

ctx.x: a way, a musician, you know. Now just go and get the hat at Royal Island, you know. And he wanted a hat, so I let him have the hat, and the man sent and got me another hat.

Yours was the first aluminum one in the city. First aluminum one I ever had, the mother had to use them derbies. But you see that aluminum don't take the place of that derby, man. No. I mean for Tone, that derby, you see that old tarlet plunging? Yeah, yeah, yeah. Man, Chris Kelly, boy, could play your old blues on that. He was the best, he was the best on that. Oh yeah, he was the best on that. That man could make you cry playing the blues. And use the glass, man. Yeah. And that wah-wah and stuff, man, them guys…
Where did you get the idea for using the glass in the first place, Tom?
